sent_bad: Flares are also hard to manage because normal pregnancy symptoms — fatigue, fluid build-up in the joints, skin changes, hair loss, shortness of breath, and joint pain — can mimic lupus symptoms, making it difficult to distinguish a flare from a normal pregnancy.
Some lupus medications (such as methotrexate, mycophenolate, or cyclophosphamide) are harmful to the baby; some can cross the placenta and pose a threat to it.
